name: BM-21 Grad

placement_rationale.text: BM-21 Grad's own operating_range_km (5–20 km) already brackets 8 km, sitting toward the shorter end of that stated envelope — appropriate for a short-range saturation system whose entire draw, per this asset's own characteristics, is being cheap and weather-independent rather than precise or deep-reaching. Doctrine.md §2 places FPV strike range at 0–10 km and close reconnaissance at 1–5 km, so 8 km keeps Grad inside the same dense forward zone those systems occupy, consistent with a weapon whose 40-rocket salvo empties in ~20 seconds and is meant to displace immediately after rather than sit at standoff. This is the shortest-ranged, most forward-sited launcher in this artillery batch, matching its role as the all-weather fallback fire support least dependent on the drone-cued precision kill chain doctrine.md documents elsewhere.

representative_system: BM-21 Grad (122mm MLRS); modernized as Tornado-G

image.license: See Commons file page for license

cost.display: ~$500K–1M per launcher vehicle (open-source estimate, wide range reflects Soviet-stock reactivation vs. newer-build pricing); each 122mm rocket costs roughly $3,000

key_facts.label: Role
key_facts.value: Unguided area-saturation fire, not precision strike

short_role: Truck-mounted unguided rocket artillery for saturating an area target — cheap per shot, imprecise per shot, still in wide use.
characteristics: 40-tube launcher can empty a full salvo in roughly 20 seconds
Unguided rockets — accuracy is area-effect, not point-precision
Tornado-G modernization adds satellite navigation and automated fire control to the same basic platform
Far cheaper per shot than any GPS-guided round, which keeps it in use despite lower per-round precision
employment_notes: Reported use has become more selective than earlier in the war — doctrine and battlefield reporting both describe artillery as used more sparingly than in the opening phases, while remaining a reliable, weather-independent tool precisely because it doesn't depend on a drone link or clear optics the way precision-guided fires do.
contrast_vs_traditional: Grad represents the fires this war's drone-centric kill chains were layered on top of, not replaced by. Even as reconnaissance-to-strike chains built around drones and precision munitions have taken over most of the targeting work, unguided saturation rocket fire remains the fallback that works in weather and jamming conditions that ground a drone — a genuinely all-weather capability the newer systems haven't fully matched.

reactive_behavior.description: On select: launcher elevates, a rocket salvo fires, brief downrange impact spread.
